nodes.label: Current vs Override Header Badge Pattern
nodes.summary: Every per-zone admin config form must show a prominent header badge on each editable field displaying the currently-applied value and whether it comes from a saved override (yellow) or the theme default (green). Prevents the 'why isn't my change visible?' confusion by surfacing override state at the field itself.

nodes.label: Green Inheriting Badge State
nodes.summary: Green badge (`bg-success/15 text-success`) labeled 'Current: <value>' indicates no override is saved; the value is measured live from the storefront probe via getComputedStyle. Editing the theme changes it; saving here pins the zone.

nodes.label: Yellow Override Badge State
nodes.summary: Yellow badge (`bg-warning/15 text-warning`) labeled 'Current: <value> · override' indicates the merchant has a saved value that shadows the theme default. Hover-title instructs how to clear it and revert.

nodes.label: Three-Tier Value Resolution (Override → Measured → Hide)
nodes.summary: Badge value resolves in priority order: (1) cfg.fontSize saved override → yellow badge; (2) measured[zone].fontSize from iframe probe → green badge; (3) neither available (probe pending or zone absent) → hide the badge entirely rather than showing '—'.

nodes.label: Storefront Probe iframe getComputedStyle Mechanism
nodes.summary: Admin page renders a hidden iframe (opacity:0, NOT display:none — display:none prevents layout resolution) loading the live storefront with ?probe=typography. The TypographyProbe component runs getComputedStyle on each data-zone element after hydration and postMessages computed styles back. Admin reads measured[zone][prop] for green-badge values.

nodes.label: Override Badge Applicable Surfaces
nodes.summary: The badge applies to any admin surface where a merchant override can shadow a platform default: Typography (font-size per zone), Branding/Theme (primary color), Layout (cardSize), Payment config (API key source), Hero banner (overlay-tint/aspect ratio). Rule: wherever override can shadow default, badge is required.

nodes.label: Override Discoverability Principle
nodes.summary: Override state must be surfaced AT the field where it causes confusion — header position is mandatory, not bottom-of-form or tooltip-only. A visible color cue is required alongside the numeric value; color distinction alone (without the value) or value alone (without color) are both insufficient.

nodes.label: Override Badge Anti-Patterns
nodes.summary: Five anti-patterns: (1) hint at bottom of form not header; (2) override state behind tooltip only, no color cue; (3) showing numeric value without green/yellow distinction; (4) removing badge when field is blank — that is precisely when inheriting state is most useful; (5) showing '—' or 'unknown' when probe hasn't responded — hide instead.

nodes.label: Override Badge Verification Recipe
nodes.summary: Four-step verification for any new config form: (1) save override → reload → yellow badge with override value; (2) clear override → reload → green badge with theme default; (3) change platform theme default → reload → green badges update across all stores; (4) set then clear override → badge flips yellow→green correctly. Any step failing = discoverability gap open.

nodes.label: Probe iframe display:none Kills Layout Trap
nodes.summary: The probe iframe must use opacity:0 + pointer-events:none + position:absolute, NOT display:none. display:none prevents the browser from performing layout, so getComputedStyle returns 0 or empty for size-dependent properties — the probe reads nothing and green badges never appear.

nodes.label: Zod Silent Strip Can Make Override Badge Show Wrong State
nodes.summary: If the API's Zod schema silently strips a field (e.g. fontSize not in the schema), the saved override is dropped server-side. The badge then reads green (theme default) when the merchant expects yellow (their override). Always cross-reference ebda-zod-silent-strip-trap when badge shows green-when-expected-yellow.
